dedupe_keys.name: gs1 epcis 2 0 and core business vocabulary cbv supply chain visibility event standard

description: EPCIS (Electronic Product Code Information Services) is the GS1 standard for creating and sharing visibility event data across supply chains, and the Core Business Vocabulary (CBV) is its companion vocabulary of business steps, dispositions and location and transaction types. Each EPCIS event records the completion of a business process step on one or more physical or digital objects (trade items, logistic units, returnable assets, documents), and the standard defines event types including object, aggregation, transaction, transformation and association events, master data, and capture and query interfaces. It is developed by GS1 AISBL through its global standards process with a large work group of GS1 member organisations, solution providers and users; Release 2.0 was ratified in June 2022. Coverage is generic and worldwide; it does not require RFID or instance-level identifiers. The specification (229 pages), XML schemas, JSON and JSON-LD bindings, REST bindings, ontologies and example data are free to download from GS1's reference site; drafts are on GitHub. Caveats: it is a data standard, not a dataset, so users need event data from supply chain partners; implementations fall under the GS1 IP Policy, which gives GS1 members a royalty-free or RAND licence to necessary claims but does not cover third-party patents; and the GS1 main website blocks this environment. EPCIS supports digital twin, network flow and resilience studies of freight and logistics chains built from shared event data, and complements the SupplyNetPy simulator and the railML and GTFS standards catalogued here.
licence: GS1 standard, free to download; implementation under the GS1 IP Policy (royalty-free or RAND licence to necessary claims for GS1 members)
